historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026 pro forma revenue guidance (+3.1-3.6%, 2026-11-04) corroborated by the 3-yr continuing-operations revenue CAGR of 3.2% (FY2022 9,720 to FY2025 10,677) and the Q3-2026 pro forma recurring revenue growth of 2.5%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is deeply negative (-20%/yr) because of the $17.6B Worldpay impairment in FY2022-23, the FY2024 disposal and $7.5B of buybacks FY2022-25; it is a capital-return and write-down artefact, not an operating growth signal, and is not used. EPS CAGRs are undefined (FY2022 EPS -27.74, FY2023 -11.26) for the same reason.
historical_growth.notes: revenue_5yr_cagr is actually the 4-yr continuing-ops figure FY2021 9,339 to FY2025 10,677 (3.4%): FY2020 revenue of 12,552 still consolidates Worldpay and is not comparable. Owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC): FY2023 1,178 (1,298-120), FY2024 1,172 (1,358-186), FY2025 1,438 (1,619-181); the 2-yr CAGR of 10.5% is flattered by FY2023-24 Worldpay-separation drag. Pre-FY2023 reported FCF (FY2022 2,880, FY2021 3,857) includes Worldpay and is not on the same series, so 3- and 5-yr FCF CAGRs are null rather than misleading. Owner FCF CAGR versus reported: FY2023-25 reported 11.7% vs owner 10.5%; SBC grew faster than cash flow (120 to 181) off a low 2023 base.

scenario_narratives.base: FIS is a 42%-margin, ~3%-growth processor whose equity is a levered stub: 20.0B of net debt against a 14.9B market cap after the Issuer Solutions purchase. Base assumes the November guide-down is the new run-rate rather than the start of a decline: pro forma revenue grows 3.5% for three years on recurring revenue (+2.5%) plus licence and cross-sell into the enlarged issuer base, fading to 2.5%; adjusted EBITDA margin expands 42 -> 43.5% as synergies land; the chronic 'acquisition, integration and other' cash costs taper from ~4% to 2.5% of revenue but never disappear; cash taxes 21-22% on unlevered EBIT; capex including deferred contract costs ~11%. Buybacks stay paused until gross leverage reaches 2.8x, so the first three years of FCF go to debt paydown, which the model captures through the net-debt deduction rather than a falling share count. Terminal value capped at 15x owner FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: Issuer Solutions delivers its synergies and the combined data set drives cross-sell: pro forma growth 5% fading to 3%, adjusted margin to 45.5%, transformation spend finally normalises to 1.5% of revenue, and a 16x terminal multiple reflects a re-rating back toward the processor peer group once deleveraging restores buybacks. Requires three independent things to go right (integration, reacceleration, multiple), hence the below-default weight.
scenario_narratives.bear: The guide-down was the first cut, not the last. Bank consolidation and in-house or AI-assisted core modernisation erode processing pricing at renewal; Issuer Solutions loses issuer clients during migration; Capital Markets licence revenue stalls. Revenue drifts down 1-2.5% a year, adjusted margin compresses to 36%, the transformation programme never ends (4-5% of revenue), and the terminal multiple is 12x. With 20B of debt ahead of the equity, a ~25% fall in enterprise value takes two-thirds off the share price; this scenario is also where covenant headroom and the investment-grade rating come into question and the dividend ($0.44/qtr, ~$910M/yr) is cut to fund deleveraging.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on a strict basis: SBC expensed at 1.4% of revenue with the share count held flat; the chronic acquisition/integration/transformation cash costs FIS excludes from Adjusted EBITDA are charged in the margin; deferred contract cost additions and financed hardware are treated as capex; purchase-accounting amortisation is excluded from D&A so tax is levied on the operating asset base; terminal value is the lower of Gordon and a 12-16x owner-FCF cap; net debt of 20.0B is deducted once at the end. FY0 is an estimate of FY2026 built from 9M actuals and reaffirmed guidance, because the FY2025 actuals predate both the acquisition and the debt that funded it. SANITY-CHECK FIX PASS 2026-11-08: the multiples check tripped on implied P/E (163x on FY2025 GAAP net income of 385M less SBC) and diagnosed peak FCF and a low WACC. One pass applied: WACC raised 8.0% -> 9.0% in every scenario (+0.5% leverage/refinancing, +0.5% regulatory/execution; see inputs.wacc_rationale). The mid-cycle FCF rebase was assessed and NOT applied because the 'median' is FY2011 FCF of a company one-third the size; on a margin basis FY2026E is inside the ten-year band (mid_cycle_fcf block). The terminal caps were verified at ~7-9x adjusted EBITDA, below the ten-year EV/EBITDA floor (exit_multiple_cap block).
key_risks_to_valuation: Leverage gearing: every $1B change in enterprise value is ~$1.93/share; the bear-base spread is almost entirely a leverage effect
Issuer Solutions integration: $13.5B purchase, controls not yet integrated, client migrations through 2027; synergy slippage shows up as both lower margin and a longer transformation-cost tail
Secular pricing pressure on core processing from bank consolidation and AI-assisted modernisation; a second guidance cut would move the base case toward the bear path
FY0 is an estimate: the FY2026 10-K (Feb 2027) replaces revenue 13,700 / adj EBITDA 5,585 / FCF 2,200 with actuals and should trigger an update
Cash tax rate: a lower-than-modelled deductible share of Issuer Solutions goodwill, or loss of interest deductibility under Sec. 163(j) caps, raises the effective cash rate

Dividend ($910M/yr) plus deleveraging consumes essentially all levered FCF through 2028; any FCF shortfall against the $2.15-2.25B guide delays the buyback restart the flat share count implicitly assumes
Terminal cap multiple: at a 15x cap the terminal value is ~55% of EV; at 12x the base value falls materially

Discount rate: at 9.0% WACC the equity is still ~2.3x geared to EV, so each further +0.5% of WACC removes roughly 3-4% of EV and 6-9% of per-share value; management's own 11.5% impairment-test rate would roughly halve the base value
valuation_philosophy.sanity_check_note: RESIDUAL TRIP AFTER FIX: implied P/E 144.9x (was 163.1x) versus a 134.6x threshold. This is a denominator artefact: FY2025 GAAP net income (385M) sits ~2.6B below adjusted net income because of ~1.2B of purchase-accounting amortisation, ~690M of acquisition/integration/transformation charges and Worldpay equity-method losses, all of which this model already charges or excludes explicitly, and the market itself traded FIS at 171x that denominator in December 2025. The multiple that is comparable across the Worldpay and Issuer Solutions restructurings is EV/EBITDA, and after the WACC change the model's implied EV/EBITDA of 11.4x and P/S of 2.77x are BELOW the lowest FIS has traded at in ten years (12.97x, 2.83x). Clearing the P/E rule would require cutting the base value a further ~7% and pushing those two multiples further under their historical floors; the fix was stopped after one pass as the protocol requires. Nothing in this pass changed a driver path; the scenario judgments stand. The ~62% weighted upside at $28.73 should be read against the bear case of $6.72: the equity is a levered stub and the dispersion, not the midpoint, is the finding.

mid_cycle_fcf.diagnosis_tested: sanity_check peak_fcf: base-year FCF 2,005.0 is 2.4x the historical median 839.8
mid_cycle_fcf.historical_median_period: FY2011 (revenue ~5.7B; the median of the FY2007-FY2023 reported-FCF series, in which FY2024 and FY2025 FCF are blank in the Metrics.csv and FY2020-FY2023 still consolidate Worldpay)
mid_cycle_fcf.latest_owner_fcf_period: FY2026E (revenue 13,700 after the 2026-01-09 Issuer Solutions acquisition added ~28% to revenue)
mid_cycle_fcf.reason_not_applied: The ratio measures a step change in company SIZE, not a cyclical peak in profitability. The 839.8 median comes from a company one-third to one-half the current revenue base, and the series mixes pre-Worldpay, Worldpay-consolidated and post-Worldpay entities. On the only comparable basis -- owner FCF as a percent of revenue -- FY2026E is inside the historical band, not above it (see margin_table). Valuing 13.7B of revenue off a 1,422 FCF base would impose a 10.4% owner-FCF margin that FIS has not recorded in any of the last ten years and would price the debt-funded acquisition's revenue at zero cash contribution while deducting the 7.7B of debt that bought it. The acquisition's cash flows and its debt must be treated symmetrically.

FY2026E.note: guidance midpoint; SBC 195 deducted; includes higher-margin Issuer Solutions

mid_cycle_fcf.what_would_change_this: If the FY2026 10-K shows company-defined FCF below ~1.9B, or the FY2027 outlook implies an owner-FCF margin under 13%, the FY0 anchor should be rebased in the FY2026 update.
mid_cycle_fcf.data_note: Metrics.csv FY2024/FY2025 FreeCashFlow and OperatingCashFlow are blank and CapEx reads 97/154 (PP&E additions only; 10-K total additions to PP&E and software were 989 in FY2025). Backfilling those rows through make fix would move the sanity check's median up materially.

exit_multiple_cap.basis: terminal_cap_multiple is expressed on owner FCF (x owner FCF, year 10). This block translates each scenario's binding terminal value into EV / company-defined Adjusted EBITDA at year 10 for comparison with the 10-yr historical EV/EBITDA range used by the sanity check (min 12.97x FY2025, avg 18.09x, max 26.22x FY2019).

base.reference: below 10yr min 12.97x; the protocol's base cap would be the 10yr avg 18.09x

bull.reference: below 10yr min 12.97x; the protocol's bull cap would be the 10yr max 26.22x

exit_multiple_cap.action: No change. Every scenario's terminal value already sits below the lowest EV/EBITDA FIS has traded at in ten years, so an EV/EBITDA cap at min/avg/max would not bind and would only loosen the model if applied in place of the FCF cap.
exit_multiple_cap.comparability_flag: FY2019-FY2021 EV/EBITDA of 17.6-26.2x is NOT comparable to today's entity: it prices the Worldpay-consolidated FIS (merchant acquiring, higher growth, 2019 deal premium) with ~28B of equity-funded goodwill. The post-divestiture FIS is a smaller, ~3%-growth, 3.7x-levered bank-software processor; the comparable range is FY2016-FY2018 and FY2023-FY2025 (13.0-16.8x). Those years are excluded from any multiple we would anchor on, which is why the 12-16x owner-FCF caps (~7-9x adjusted EBITDA) are retained rather than loosened to the 18-26x the protocol table would allow.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.

diagnosis.detail: Base year FCF 2,005.0 is 2.4x the historical median 839.8
Structural risks in the qualitative analysis that a standard WACC may not price: cyclicality, regulatory single point of failure

sanity_check.fix_applied: 2026-11-08 one-pass fix per research-stock Step 8c.5. Applied: WACC 8.0% -> 9.0% in all scenarios (+0.5% leverage/refinancing premium, +0.5% regulatory/execution premium; inputs.wacc_rationale). Assessed and NOT applied: mid-cycle FCF rebase (mid_cycle_fcf block: the 839.8 'median' is FY2011 FCF of a company one-third the size; FY2026E owner-FCF margin 14.6% is inside the ten-year 10-15% band). Verified, no change: terminal caps translate to 5.4x / 8.0x / 9.2x adjusted EBITDA (bear/base/bull), all below the ten-year EV/EBITDA minimum of 12.97x (exit_multiple_cap block). No driver path was changed.

inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2026E company-defined free cash flow (OCF less additions to PP&E and software, excluding ~$477M of cash transaction taxes on the Worldpay sale): midpoint of the FY2026 outlook of $2,150-2,250M reaffirmed 2026-11-04. 9M-2026 actual on the same basis was 1,861 (8-K ex99.1 Exhibit F); FY2025 actual was 1,619 (OCF 2,608 less capex 989, 10-K lines 3633-3636). This is a LEVERED figure: it is after ~$830M/yr of cash interest on the post-deal debt. The engine's component build projects UNLEVERED owner FCF and deducts net debt at the end, so year-1 projected FCF (~2.9B) sits above last_fcf by roughly the after-tax interest; that is by design, not a discontinuity.

inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-06T21:00:02Z regular close (Friday); not an after-hours print
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rates. Mechanical build: cost of equity ~9.5% (10-yr UST ~4.2%, beta ~1.05, ERP 5.0%); pre-tax cost of debt ~5.2% (2026 senior notes; portfolio effective rate 3.9%), after-tax ~4.1%; at management's TARGET structure (gross leverage ~2.8x, ~35% debt / 65% equity at intrinsic value) WACC = 7.6%, rounded to the 8.0% house floor for a levered mid-cap processor. 2026-11-08 sanity-check fix pass (wacc_too_low diagnosis): two additive premiums are charged on top of the 8.0% base, giving 9.0%. (1) +0.5% leverage/refinancing premium: actual gross leverage is ~3.7x (net ~3.5x) against the 2.8x target the 7.6% calculation assumed, $5.6B of commercial paper and current maturities must be refinanced at ~5.2% against a 3.9% portfolio rate, buybacks are suspended until deleveraging, and with 20.0B of net debt ahead of a ~15B equity the equity is carrying refinancing and rating risk (BBB, negative outlook) that target-weight WACC arithmetic ignores. (2) +0.5% regulatory/execution premium: FIS is a critical third-party provider to US and EU banks (DORA critical-ICT designation, FFIEC supervision), i.e. a regulatory single point of failure whose remediation costs are non-discretionary; the Issuer Solutions integration is running with un-integrated internal controls over 19% of revenue; and bank-sector cyclicality flows through licence and professional-services revenue. Cross-checks: management's own Banking reporting-unit impairment-test discount rate was 11.5% including a company-specific premium (10-Q line 3836), so 9.0% sits between the mechanical 7.6% and management's 11.5%. At today's market-value weights (58% debt) the mechanical WACC would be ~6.4%; that is the distressed-equity weighting and is not used. Overlap note: the guidance cut and the CFO departure are priced in the 30% bear weight, not here, to avoid charging the same risk twice.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A): US GAAP operating lease cost is already inside Adjusted EBITDA (so inside the modelled margin); lease liabilities are therefore NOT added to net debt. No lease_cost_pct_path.
inputs.ebitda_margin_definition: ebitda_margin_path is OWNER pre-SBC cash EBITDA margin = Adjusted EBITDA margin (company definition, which is already after SBC expense) + SBC % of revenue - a recurring charge for 'acquisition, integration and other costs'. FIS has booked $500-700M of these every year (FY2025 689 = 6.5% of revenue, 10-K line ~5352; 9M-2026 532 = 5.3%; 9M-2025 503), of which 'enterprise transformation initiatives' alone were 342 in 9M-2026. They are excluded from Adjusted EBITDA but are real, chronic cash costs and are charged here, tapering as Issuer Solutions integration completes but never to zero. FY2026E anchor: adjusted margin 40.8% (guided adjusted EBITDA $5,565-5,605M / ~13,700; 9M actual 41.4%, Q3 42.9%, so the guide implies a soft Q4 of ~1,390) + SBC 1.4% - charge 5.1% (~700) = 37.1%. Base year-1: 41.3 + 1.4 - 4.0 = 38.7%.
inputs.capex_definition: capex_pct_path covers additions to PP&E and software (FY2026E ~1,090 = 8.0%; FY2025 989 = 9.3%) PLUS the recurring cash additions to deferred contract costs (FY2025 469, FY2024 509, 9M-2026 292; ~3% of revenue), whose amortisation sits inside the D&A line, PLUS ~1% for hardware and software bought under financing arrangements (FY2025 185, repaid through financing activities). da_pct_path is D&A EXCLUDING purchase-accounting amortisation (FY2025 1,215 = 11.4%; 9M-2026 1,038 = 10.3% of revenue) so that EBIT and cash tax are built on the operating asset base; the ~$1.2B/yr of acquired-intangible amortisation is non-cash and its deductible slice is reflected in the sub-statutory cash tax rate.
inputs.fy0_estimate_note: FY0 is an ESTIMATE (FY2026E) because the valuation sits seven weeks before year-end and FY2025 actuals (revenue 10,677, adj EBITDA 4,331, FCF 1,619) describe a company without Issuer Solutions and with a $13.1B rather than $20.8B debt stack. FY2026E anchors: revenue 13,700; adjusted EBITDA ~5,585 (guided $5,565-5,605M; 9M 4,195, so Q4E ~1,390); SBC ~195; acquisition/integration/other ~700; D&A ex-PPA ~1,400; capex ~1,090; deferred contract cost additions ~400; cash taxes ex-Worldpay-transaction ~250 (9M paid 571 of which ~477 were Worldpay transaction taxes). Replace with 10-K actuals in the FY2026 update.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md row 1, operating company). FIS is a software/processing vendor TO banks, not a deposit-taker: its revenue is recurring processing fees and licences, it has no deposits or loan book, and its cash flow statement means what the engine assumes. First valuation; no memory entry. Business: Banking Solutions (core processing, digital, payments, and from 2026-01-09 the ex-Global Payments Issuer Solutions card-issuer processing business, rebranded FIS Total Issuing) and Capital Market Solutions (trading, lending, treasury and risk software). Worldpay: 55% sold to GTCR 2024-01-31; the remaining 45% was sold to Global Payments on 2026-01-09 for $5,762M of value applied against the $13,473M Issuer Solutions purchase price, with $7,695M cash (debt-funded) making up the difference; Q1-2026 GAAP earnings carry the ~$2.2B after-tax remeasurement gain and must not be read as operating profit. Segments were recast in 2026 (Issuer Solutions into Banking plus reclassifications), so FY2025 segment rows on the old basis in the kpis table are not comparable with 2026 rows. Guidance history 2026: Feb outlook pro forma revenue +5.1-5.7%, adj EBITDA +7.2-8.4%, adj EPS +8-10%; Nov outlook pro forma revenue +3.1-3.6%, adj EBITDA +2.9-3.6%, adj EPS +1.2-2.4% ($5.82-5.89 vs $6.15-6.24 prior; adjusted revenue $13,445-13,505M vs $13,630-13,695M; adjusted EBITDA $5,565-5,605M), FCF raised to $2.15-2.25B. Management attributed the cut to banking recurring-revenue softness, client conversion delays and bank consolidation (FIS_Analysis.json, guidance block). CFO James Kehoe stepped down effective 2026-11-05 (10-Q Item 5). Price fell from ~$65 in Dec-2025 to $37.5 in late Oct-2026 and 23% further in the week of the Q3 print, to a 52-week low. Market cap ~14.9B against net debt 20.0B: the equity is a levered stub, so EV moves are amplified ~2.3x in the share price, which is why the bear weight is above the house default. Horizon 10 years: the owner margin is still ramping through year 5 as integration costs taper.

bear.ebitda_margin_note: Adjusted margin 40.3 -> 36.0% as renewal pricing concessions, Issuer Solutions client attrition and a fixed cost base bite, while the recurring charge stays 5.0 -> 4.0% because the transformation never ends. Capex cannot be cut below ~11% without accelerating attrition.
bear.wacc_note: 9.0% = 8.0% house base + 0.5% leverage/refinancing premium + 0.5% regulatory/execution premium; see inputs.wacc_rationale. Same rate in every scenario: the scenario paths and weights carry path risk, the WACC carries the cost of capital.

base.ebitda_margin_note: Adjusted EBITDA margin 41.3 -> 43.0% by year 5 from the FY2026E anchor of 40.8% (guided adjusted EBITDA $5,565-5,605M on ~13,700 revenue; Issuer Solutions mix, ~$150M cost synergies, operating leverage) plus SBC 1.4%, less recurring acquisition/integration/transformation cash costs 4.0 -> 2.5% of revenue. Owner margin matures by year 5.
base.growth_note: 3.5% for three years = top of the cut FY2026 pro forma range (3.1-3.6%), then fading to 2.5% terminal: recurring revenue is growing 2.5%, bank consolidation is a persistent headwind, and licence/professional-services revenue is lumpy.
base.tax_note: 21% rising to 22%: FIS's adjusted effective tax rate has run ~20-22%; part of the Issuer Solutions goodwill is deductible for US federal tax, and the rate applies to unlevered EBIT (the interest tax shield belongs in WACC, not here).
base.wc_note: Growth consumes a little cash: receivables and prepaid balances rose with revenue in FY2025 and 9M-2026 while deferred revenue was flat, so a -5% capture on the revenue change.
base.wacc_note: 9.0% = 8.0% house base + 0.5% leverage/refinancing premium + 0.5% regulatory/execution premium; see inputs.wacc_rationale. Same rate in every scenario: the scenario paths and weights carry path risk, the WACC carries the cost of capital.

bull.ebitda_margin_note: Adjusted margin 41.8 -> 45.0% (full Issuer Solutions synergies plus Capital Markets mix at 52-54%) and the recurring charge falls 3.5 -> 1.5% as transformation spend finally normalises.
bull.wacc_note: 9.0% = 8.0% house base + 0.5% leverage/refinancing premium + 0.5% regulatory/execution premium; see inputs.wacc_rationale. Same rate in every scenario: the scenario paths and weights carry path risk, the WACC carries the cost of capital.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30%: gross leverage ~3.7x and net ~3.5x adjusted EBITDA makes equity value a ~2.3x-geared function of enterprise value; FY2026 guidance was cut materially within nine months of being set (pro forma EBITDA growth 7.2-8.4% to 2.9-3.6%); the CFO departed the week of the Q3 print; Issuer Solutions internal controls are not yet integrated (19% of revenue, 33% of assets); and the stock sits at a 52-week low on a P/E near 5x, which says the market's own weight on a decline scenario is already high. Bull cut to 20% because it needs integration, reacceleration and a re-rating simultaneously. Base 50%: the business is 80% recurring with $24.5B of remaining performance obligations and FCF guidance was raised, not cut, so a stable-at-lower-growth outcome remains the single most likely path.
